items.followUp: State one similarity and one difference between Dobereiner’s triads and Newlands’ law of octaves.

rubric.why: A triad is a group of three elements with similar properties.
rubric.description: Identifies a triad as three elements with similar properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the group contains three elements with similar chemical properties.

rubric.why: The atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the other two.
rubric.description: States the atomic-mass relationship within a triad.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the middle element’s atomic mass is approximately the mean of the other two.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner arranged some elements in groups of three, called triads, whose elements had similar chemical properties.
In each triad, the atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the other two elements.

items.followUp: Explain how inner-shell electrons affect the attraction between the nucleus and valence electrons.

rubric.why: Inner-shell electrons shield outer electrons from the nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies inner-shell electrons as the cause of shielding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying inner-shell electrons as shielding the outer electrons.

rubric.why: Shielding reduces the effective attraction of the nucleus on valence electrons.
rubric.description: States that shielding reduces the attraction experienced by valence electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the attraction between the nucleus and valence electrons is reduced.

modelAnswer: The shielding effect is the reduction in the attraction between the nucleus and valence electrons due to the presence of inner-shell electrons.
The inner electrons shield the outer electrons from the positive charge of the nucleus.

items.followUp: Write two properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points because of the strong electrostatic forces between their ions.
rubric.description: Gives the high melting and boiling points of ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionic compounds have high melting points and high boiling points.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state.
rubric.description: Gives an electrical-conductivity property of ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating conductivity when molten or aqueous, or lack of conductivity in the solid state.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds generally have high melting points and high boiling points.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but do not conduct electricity in the solid state.
